title: bug: nothing stops an agent session's porcelain `git commit` in the shared control checkout — a subagent's failed `cd` committed 4 peers' WIP as "D" and a landing pushed it
description:
Incident on 2026-10-30 at 13:27:12Z: worker-0062feec (task-30066ccd, WT-S) launched a review subagent. The subagent ran a scratch command in the repo root after its `cd` into a scratch dir failed, and that command made commit f6da2d7f "D" on moe/work-2026-10-24. The commit took every modified or staged tracked file, 71 in all:
- unreviewed in-progress bytes from task-f31d415d (scripts/moe-agent.sh/.ps1, postflight.sh), task-b1aecb54 (proposeRail.ts/.test.ts, docs), task-71516084 (local-runner) and WT-S;
- 2 human-staged root files;
- 57 .moe/ paths.

Two minutes later the next wrapper landing (91eaa6ae) pushed it to origin. Every idle sh seat then hot-reloaded the unreviewed wrapper bytes, because 5998f871 now trusts "committed" bytes. Each affected task's own landing found its paths already clean, so per-task attribution and QA's commit evidence broke.

The rule "wrappers are the only Git writers" is prompt-only. Nothing in the checkout enforces it.

Expected: a porcelain `git commit` (and, ideally, `git push`) run from inside an agent session in the control checkout is refused, with a message saying the wrapper lands the work.
- The wrapper's own landings must still work. A human committing outside any agent session must still work.
- One possible shape: a hook installed via core.hooksPath pointing at a tracked hooks dir, which refuses when MOE_WORKER_ID (or a dedicated marker the wrappers export to CLIs) is set and the wrapper's landing marker is not. The architect decides the shape.
- Account for both launchers (sh and ps1 twins) and for the settings.commitHooks semantics.
definitionOfDone: Inside a launched agent session (sh and ps1 seats), a porcelain `git commit` in the control checkout is refused with a message naming the wrapper landing rule. A regression test reproduces the 2026-10-30 shape: a scratch command run in the control checkout after a failed cd.
Wrapper completion and checkpoint landings, and a human's commit made outside any agent session, still succeed. Postflight harnesses (sh and ps1) and the parity check pass.
docs (scripts/CLAUDE.md Land on every exit, plus TROUBLESHOOTING) describe the guard and how a human bypasses it deliberately.

The fake CLI deliberately runs a nested shell with a failed scratch cd followed by ordinary git commit -am D (without errexit), plus staged-only commit, and attempts a push to a disposable local bare remote. implementationPlan.description: Implement twin agent Git-guard preparation using native Git process-scoped configuration, never persistent git config or installed-hook replacement. Resolve the control checkout's absolute gitdir and existing effective hook directory BEFORE adding the overlay. In a per-seat secure temp directory generate LF/no-BOM shell hooks and a tiny config setting core.hooksPath. Append an includeIf.gitdir:<exact escaped absolute control gitdir>.path entry through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n; use Git-compatible Windows paths/case handling, no trailing-slash recursive match, and escape Git wildmatch/config/shell syntax independently. Existing caller config entries remain intact. Generate pre-commit/pre-push refusal hooks with MOE_AGENT_GIT_REFUSED and 'the wrapper lands the work'; only explicit MOE_ALLOW_AGENT_GIT_WRITES=1 delegates to the original hook. Forward other installed executable hooks to their original absolute files with unchanged args/stdin/status, not copied bodies or eval. Preserve original hook failures on bypass. Validate the effective hooksPath using the actual prospective child env. Error handling: failed identity/config/temp/permission/validation means MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED and no CLI launch, never an unprotected fallback. Non-Git projects remain supported without claiming Git protection.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented matching native Git conditional-include preparation in both wrappers using existing Node runtime and stdlib, LF/no-BOM forwarding hooks, independently escaped wildmatch/config/shell paths, original absolute hooks resolved before overlay, inherited runtime configuration append, and prospective-child hooksPath validation. Non-Git returns no overlay; errors are redacted/fail closed. bash -n passes; actual embedded preparation probe in an absolute disposable Unicode/glob/metacharacter repo passed (refusal exit 1, wrapper-rule diagnostic, no installed-hook modification). Full-wrapper RED remains until step 3 launch wiring. Bash rewritten by syntax-checked atomic rename, PS BOM preserved.

implementationPlan.description: Apply the prepared environment at every real CLI invocation (Claude/Codex/Gemini/Grok/custom command, interactive/headless, taskless notification and loop/reload paths), preserving command args, stdin/TTY, pipeline exit status and account environment. Use child subshell scope on sh; PS saves/restores only its own appended runtime-config entries in a finally before wrapper postflight/teardown, including launch failure/cancellation. Do not globally export the guard into wrapper Git or sidecars. Extend the new tests to prove normal completion with commitHooks=false and true, checkpoint plumbing, original hook denial, explicit one-command human bypass, ordinary human commit outside the session, concurrent seats with separate guard temps, and caller GIT_CONFIG_COUNT restoration (including existing core.hooksPath). Verify spawned descendant shells inherit the guard; document explicit env/config stripping as deliberate bypass, not a sandbox guarantee. Reuse existing secure-temp lifecycle; no .moe writes, no PATH git shim, no general Git protocol changes. Keep guard files alive through the CLI and remove only the seat's own temp files after exit.
implementationPlan.note: Wired all Claude/custom, Codex (including argv probe), Gemini and Grok interactive/headless launches through child-only guard environment. Bash export lives in exec subshell; PS saves/restores only the appended three variables in finally, before postflight, retaining preexisting unused entries too. Unique per-seat guard temps removed after CLI/outer cleanup; Windows root ACL restricted to current SID. Tests: Linux 19/19; native Windows PS5.1 17/17 plus new plumbing-completion/launch-failure 2/2; parity passes. Coverage includes sentinel preservation, ordinary human writes, one-command bypass + original hook rejection, forwarded args/stdin/resource-relative $0, non-Git stdin, precedence/count/setup refusal, taskless notifications, native argv, concurrent seat lifetimes, hookful/plumbing completions/checkpoints, failure exit 23 and caller env restoration. Persistent core.hooksPath install would race seats and alter human hooks; MOE_WORKER_ID alone also reaches wrapper hook-enabled commits; PATH git shims miss absolute Git and are unnecessary. Optional push guard shares the same small mechanism. No API/schema change.

Existing postflight-fake-proxy.js can supply all fixture behavior without edits. Official Git githooks/git-config document config precedence, gitdir matching and bypass limits.
